note_claims.claim: The patient is presenting with vomiting and diarrhoea since last night.
The patient has had about five non-bilious, milky vomits since last night, with fewer today.
The patient has had six to seven loose stools today.
The patient has no blood in her stools, although her brother had blood in his stool with a similar illness last week.
The patient's brother had a similar illness from nursery, and the patient attends the same nursery.
The patient has had two wet nappies since this morning.
The patient is taking small amounts of breast milk and formula.
The patient's temperature this morning was 37.4 °C.
The patient is alert and playing.
The patient is not drowsy or floppy.
The patient has no regular medications and no known drug allergies.
The assessment was conducted over the phone and no physical examination was performed.
The clinical impression is probable viral gastroenteritis with reduced urine output.
A face-to-face assessment is scheduled for the surgery today at 16:00.
The patient should continue breastfeeding and receive small amounts of oral rehydration solution (e.g., Dioralyte) every few minutes.
The patient should call 999 if she becomes floppy, very sleepy, or hard to wake.
The patient should attend A&E if her vomit goes green or if she sees blood in her nappy.

findings.note_span: Probable viral gastroenteritis with reduced urine output.
findings.transcript_evidence: It sounds like gastroenteritis, a tummy bug, probably the same one her brother had.
findings.rationale: The specific clinical finding of 'reduced urine output' is missing from the impression, although the context is implied by the discussion of wet nappies.
